### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications in `intel_ddi.c` and `intel_dpio_phy.c` are related in that they both address the handling of the DDI PHY power state. The change in `intel_ddi.c` enhances the check for the PHY's power state by including the common lane power down flag, which is crucial for accurately determining whether the PHY is powered on. Meanwhile, the removal of the port mask function and the associated checks in `intel_dpio_phy.c` simplifies the code by eliminating redundant checks that are now handled in the updated logic in `intel_ddi.c`. This results in a more streamlined approach to managing the PHY's power state, particularly in scenarios where the PHY may be incorrectly reported as powered down.

You will be given the root cause of a bug, the commit message and the corresponding patch.
        You need to extract all code statements that lead to the bug from the patch, based on the root cause and the commit message.

        Root cause:
        The bug arises from the incorrect handling of the common lane power down flag in the DPIO PHY, which can lead to the system mistakenly believing that the PHY is powered down when it is actually powered on. This misinterpretation occurs after module reloading, causing the GRC readout code to disable the PHY, resulting in the AUX power well for the PHY being left in a stuck state. The initial enabling of the PHY does not provide clarity on its power state, leading to erroneous checks and subsequent failures in power management.
        
        Commit message:
        drm/i915: Fix DDI PHY init if it was already on

The common lane power down flag of a DPIO PHY has a funky semantic:
after the initial enabling of the PHY (so from a disabled state) this
flag will be clear. It will be set only after the PHY will be used for
the first time (for instance due to enabling the corresponding pipe) and
then become unused (due to disabling the pipe). During the initial PHY
enablement we don't know which of the above phases we are in, so move
the check for the flag where this is known, the HW readout code. This is
where the rest of lane power down status checks are done anyway.

This fixes at least a problem on GLK where after module reloading, the
common lane power down flag of PHY1 is set, but the PHY is actually
powered-on and properly set up. The GRC readout code for other PHYs will
hence think that PHY1 is not powered initially and disable it after the
GRC readout. This will cause the AUX power well related to PHY1 to get
disabled in a stuck state, timing out when we try to enable it later.

Cc: Ville Syrjala <ville.syrjala@linux.intel.com>
